value.heading: Newman Catholic @ Ramapo
value.text: Newman Catholic is a student organization that seeks to create a community where we learn about and explore the Catholic Christian faith. We offer Sunday Mass, weekday Mass and Eucharistic Adoration, Bible studies, Newman Nights, OCIA (Order of Christian Initiation for Adults) classes, service opportunities, retreats, opportunities for the Sacrament of Confession and spiritual direction, and more. Wherever you are at your faith journey, we are here for you and would love to accompany you. For more information, please visit our website (https://www.ramaponewman.com/) or contact us at campusministry@ramapo.edu. (mailto:campusministry@ramapo.edu)

value.heading: Hillel
value.text: Hillel is an international organization that serves Jewish students on college campuses. Hillel offers religious and cultural programs including trips, holiday observances, historical commemorations, lectures, films, and leadership and personal growth opportunities. Although Hillel is a Jewish-based organization, it’s open to students of all faiths. They hold weekly meetings with kosher food, have dinners at students’ apartments and attend concerts. They provide students with volunteer opportunities as well as Shabbat and other holiday celebrations at the Rabbi’s house. Hillel provides students a great way to connect with each other on campus, as well as learn about Judaism on a religious, philosophical, and cultural level. Email: hillel@ramapo.edu (mailto:hillel@ramapo.edu)

value.heading: Chabad
value.text: Chabad is your Jewish home when you’re away from home! Chabad provides fun Jewish experiences and learning opportunities to the students at Ramapo College within the framework of traditional Judaism. Need someone to talk to? Rabbi Kaplan and Mimi Kaplan of Chabad of NW Bergen County are here for you. Want to connect or hang out with fellow Jewish students? Come on over. Are you not feeling well? Hot chicken soup is a text away. Whatever you need, we’re family and here for you. See you soon! Email: chabad@ramapo.edu (mailto:chabad@ramapo.edu)

value.heading: Syriac Orthodox Club
value.text: The Syriac Orthodox Club at Ramapo College is a community dedicated to celebrating and preserving the rich heritage of the Syriac Orthodox Christian faith. Our mission is to create a welcoming and inclusive space where students can deepen their understanding of Syriac spirituality, culture, and traditions while fostering unity and friendship. Through prayer, cultural events, and discussions, we aim to explore the beauty of the Syriac Orthodox Church’s teachings, its historical significance, and its relevance in the modern world. Whether you’re looking to connect with fellow believers, learn about an ancient Christian tradition, or simply engage in meaningful dialogue, we invite you to join us. Together, we strive to strengthen our faith, build community, and make a positive impact on campus and beyond. Everyone is welcome to participate and learn! Email:soc@ramapo.edu (mailto:soc@ramapo.edu)

question: are there cultural clubs or greek life here? whats the process to rush a sorority

body.answer:
Yes. The directory includes Greek life and cultural student groups. Cultural groups listed include Culture Club (https://archway.ramapo.edu/CultClub/), Students of Caribbean Ancestry (https://archway.ramapo.edu/SOCA/), Black Student Union (https://archway.ramapo.edu/BSU/), South Asian Club (https://archway.ramapo.edu/SAC/), African Federation of Representation and Opportunity (https://archway.ramapo.edu/afros/), Association of Latinos Moving Ahead (https://archway.ramapo.edu/ALMA/), Filipino American Student Association (https://archway.ramapo.edu/FASA/), Organization of Latino Unity (https://archway.ramapo.edu/OLU/), and United Asian Association (https://archway.ramapo.edu/UAA/); each is a Student Organization. [38–46] The culturally based organizations also include Balkan Student Association. [35]

To rush/join a sorority:
1. Complete the Greek Life Interest Form: https://cglink.me/2fF/s33074. It provides information about NPHC, PFC, IFC, CPH and UCGC. [26]
2. Eligibility: have earned 12–23 Ramapo credits or more and a cumulative GPA of at least 2.5, or 24 Ramapo credits or more and a cumulative GPA of at least 2.25; be in good academic standing, not on disciplinary probation, and a full-time enrolled student. Transfer students may join in their first semester without other eligibility requirements if in good standing. [27]
3. Attend one in-person Hazing Prevention Workshop, sign the New Member Process Acknowledgment, and complete required online courses assigned by the Coordinator of Fraternities, Sororities, and Student Organizations. [27]
Formal recruitment for NPC member sororities is in spring semester and follows NPC guidelines. [29] After spring recruitment, CPH chapters below TOTAL may continue giving bids through Continuous Open Bidding. [30]
Contact the Office of Fraternity and Sorority Life: ofsl@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7123, SC-202B. [26–27]

Sources: [26](https://www.ramapo.edu/greek/recruitment/) [27](https://www.ramapo.edu/greek/recruitment/) [29](https://www.ramapo.edu/greek/glossary-of-greek-terms/) [30](https://www.ramapo.edu/greek/glossary-of-greek-terms/) [35](https://www.ramapo.edu/oabc/home/you-belong-at-ramapo/)
